brief.headline: SK Hynix valuation flips Samsung for first time; HBM3E carries 2026, memory spot up 63% MoM, CoWoS still tight
brief.summary: <cite index="22-1,22-22">SK Hynix forward PER topped Samsung Electronics for the first time (6.79x vs 6.77x) as shares hit record 1.976M won, reversing a 2.8-point gap from three months ago</cite>. <cite index="4-10,6-1">HBM3E will account for ~66-67% of total HBM shipments in 2026 with SK Hynix holding 50%+ market share, while HBM4 gradually ramps</cite>. <cite index="11-1,15-4">DRAM contract prices jumped 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026 following Q1's 90-95% surge; NAND flash rose 63% MoM to early May per Korean customs data</cite>. <cite index="10-4,10-12">Samsung and SK Hynix raised HBM3E prices ~20% for 2026 as NVIDIA H200 China approval and hyperscaler ASIC demand (Google TPU v7, Amazon Trainium3) keep supply tight despite HBM4 entry</cite>. <cite index="31-1,31-4">Top-5 hyperscalers committed $660-690B capex for 2026, nearly doubling 2025, with 75% targeting AI infrastructure</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="22-20,25-12">SK Hynix returned 78.68% over one month vs Samsung's 35.44%, more than double</cite>. <cite index="22-22,25-14">With forward PER now converged (6.79x vs 6.77x), the valuation gap that supported Hynix's re-rating has closed</cite>. <cite index="25-19,22-2">Analysts flag that with earnings and valuations now on the same level, it will be difficult for SK Hynix to continue posting gains more than twice as large as Samsung's going forward</cite>. Samsung catching bid on relative value and strike-risk fade; <cite index="26-2,26-4,26-7">UBS projects Samsung could reach HBM market share parity with SK Hynix by 2027E, raising 2027 shipment estimates to 23Gb (up from 20.3Gb prior) while trimming SK Hynix 2026/2027 forecasts</cite>. Near-term: pair converging, take profit Hynix / add Samsung on dips. Medium-term: watch HBM4 qual cycles—Samsung gap-close is the 2H26-1H27 narrative.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="11-1,17-1">DRAM contract prices rose 90-95% QoQ in Q1 2026, then 58-63% in Q2 2026</cite>. <cite index="5-23,5-24">HBM is crowding out commodity DRAM capacity; Micron noted a 3-to-1 conversion ratio between HBM and DDR5 wafer capacity, meaning every HBM ramp directly compresses general-purpose memory supply</cite>. <cite index="6-9,6-8">Some analysts warn HBM prices could enter a correction phase after 2026 as competition heats up and capacity expands; caution is rising over pricing, supply, and geopolitical risks</cite>. <cite index="16-5,16-27">Samsung and SK Hynix, which together account for ~70% of global DRAM, signaled they do not plan aggressive capacity expansion; suppliers are actively managing scarcity, not racing to solve it, locking in customers with allocation-only frameworks that favor hyperscalers and large OEMs</cite>. Pricing power remains with suppliers through 2026; meaningful capacity relief unlikely until late 2027-2028.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="4-1,4-8,4-10">HBM3E expected to account for approximately two-thirds of total HBM shipments in 2026, remaining the flagship product; Major research and brokerage analysts expect HBM3E to account for approximately two-thirds of total HBM shipments in 2026, while HBM4 gradually increases its share</cite>. <cite index="4-12,4-13">SK Hynix maintains dominant position with 62% share of HBM shipments as of Q2 2025 and 57% of revenue as of Q3; Goldman Sachs assessed that SK hynix will maintain its dominant position in HBM3 and HBM3E until at least 2026, sustaining total HBM market share over 50%</cite>. <cite index="4-18">UBS predicts SK hynix will achieve approximately 70% market share in the HBM4 market for NVIDIA's next-generation Rubin platform in 2026</cite>. <cite index="9-2,9-5,9-6">SK hynix debuted 16-layer HBM4 with 48GB at CES 2026, representing next generation of its 12-layer HBM4 (36GB) which demonstrated industry-leading speeds of 11.7 Gbps, currently under development in line with customer schedules</cite>. <cite index="8-11,8-12">NVIDIA reportedly asked major memory suppliers whether they could deliver 16-layer HBM in Q4 2026; discussions remain exploratory with no contracts signed, but have triggered internal planning around development schedules and yield targets</cite>. <cite index="7-4,7-8">Samsung held 35% HBM market share in Q3 2025 vs SK Hynix 53%; Samsung co-CEO said 'customers have even stated that Samsung is back' on HBM4</cite>. HBM3E pricing +20% for 2026, HBM4 transition accelerates 2H26.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix forward PER overtakes Samsung for first time at 6.79x vs 6.77x
news_pulse.implication: Valuation convergence signals SK Hynix re-rating exhausted near-term; relative value now favors Samsung. Watch for rotation.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix raised HBM3E prices ~20% for 2026 as H200 China approval, hyperscaler ASIC demand surge
news_pulse.implication: HBM3E ASPs holding firm despite HBM4 ramp; tight supply through 2026 supports margin expansion for both.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM contract prices +58-63% QoQ Q2 2026, NAND +70-75%; PC DRAM doubled QoQ in Q1
news_pulse.implication: Memory supercycle intact; HBM capacity reallocation crushes commodity supply. Server DRAM and eSSD remain priority allocations.

news_pulse.headline: NAND flash prices +63% MoM to early May 2026 per Korean customs (up 351.6% YoY)
news_pulse.implication: Enterprise SSD demand absorbing all incremental NAND capacity; consumer spot falling but contract pricing still rising.

news_pulse.headline: UBS: Samsung to reach HBM market share parity with SK Hynix by 2027E; raises Samsung 2027 HBM to 23Gb
news_pulse.implication: Samsung HBM4 qual progress accelerating; 2027 share gains could pressure SK Hynix premium. Capex pull-ins driving revision.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler capex $660-690B for 2026, nearly double 2025; ~75% ($450B+) targets AI infrastructure
news_pulse.implication: Demand backstop for HBM, CoWoS, and high-capacity server DRAM/eSSD through 2027. Supply remains constraint, not demand.

news_pulse.headline: NVIDIA secured ~60-70% of TSMC CoWoS-L capacity for 2025-2026; capacity target 130k wpm by end-2026
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS remains bottleneck for AI accelerator shipments. NVIDIA allocation locks in Blackwell/Rubin supply; AMD, Broadcom fight for remaining 30-40%.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix debuted 16-layer 48GB HBM4 at CES 2026; 12-layer HBM4 at 11.7 Gbps under customer qual
news_pulse.implication: SK Hynix maintains HBM4 technology lead; 16-layer timing aligns with NVIDIA Rubin Ultra if demand materializes late 2026.

brief.derivatives_signal: <cite index="21-7,21-8,21-9">DRAM ETF (major holdings: SK Hynix 25.95%, Samsung 20.27%, Micron 6.41%) had net assets of $6.66B as of May 11; over past month net inflows totaled $4.67B, reaching $2.55B over past week, marking second-largest weekly inflow among U.S. equity ETFs trailing only SPY</cite>. <cite index="21-10,21-11,21-12">REX Shares pursuing listing of T-Rex 2X Long SK Hynix Daily Target ETF tracking twice daily return of SK Hynix ADRs; in domestic market, single-stock leveraged and inverse-2x ETFs based on Samsung and SK Hynix will launch later this month (May 27)</cite>. <cite index="21-14">Analyst estimate: inflows into Samsung and SK Hynix leveraged ETFs expected to reach 1.7 trillion won conservative, 5.3 trillion won aggressive</cite>. Retail euphoria building; levered products launch signals local top risk. Fade strength.
